chunks: Salat (prayer), sawm (fasting), hajj (pilgrimage), charity, righteousness, and du'a (supplication) enter upon the deceased in his grave, and its reward is written for the one who performs it and for the deceased.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: charity given such that its benefit reaches the deceased
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer) offered on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm (fasting) whose reward reaches the deceased
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: hajj (pilgrimage) performed with reward for the deceased
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave, the place where the deceased receives the benefit

ai.seo_question: Do salat, fasting, hajj, charity, and supplication benefit the deceased in the grave?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that acts of devotion and goodness performed on behalf of the deceased benefit them in the grave. The reward is recorded both for the person performing the act and for the deceased, highlighting the continuing benefit of worship, charity, and supplication after death.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, charity, righteousness, and supplication enter upon the deceased in their grave, and the reward is written for both the one who performs these deeds and the deceased."
